name: @shani/ui
description: Machine-readable and developer-facing metadata manifest for Shani Design System components

components.name: Box
components.description: Atomic layout primitive providing tokenized padding, margin, surface backgrounds, borders, shadows, and flex constraints without hardcoded styling.
whenToUse: Use Box for atomic layout containment and surface-level background styling.
Use token-mapped padding and margin shorthand (p, px, py, m) instead of raw style objects.
Use for cards, containers, and badges that require tokenized borders, radii, or shadows.
whenNotToUse: Never use Box with arbitrary pixel numbers; stick to strict spacing tokens (1=4pt, 2=8pt, etc.).
Never use raw hex colors or inline style overrides for background colors; use bg="surface", bg="brand", etc.
accessibilityNotes: Box passes through accessibility props directly to the underlying View without interfering with screen readers.
Ensure background surface contrast matches or exceeds WCAG AA against foreground text.

components.name: Stack
components.description: Directional layout primitive enforcing the strict 4pt spacing scale between child elements with optional divider injection.
whenToUse: Use Stack for linear content spacing instead of manual margin calculations.
Use tokenized spacing values (2, 3, 4, 6) to keep screens strictly aligned on the 4pt grid.
Use the divider prop for automated separator injection between adjacent children.
whenNotToUse: Never hardcode raw pixel margins (e.g. marginBottom: 13) on children inside a Stack.
Never mix arbitrary flexbox alignment props on container views when Stack provides align and justify.
accessibilityNotes: Stack passes through accessibility props without interfering with the screen reader reading order.
Non-interactive dividers injected by Stack automatically hide from assistive tech.

components.name: HStack
components.description: Horizontal stack layout enforcing consistent spacing between horizontal items with optional divider injection and wrap support.
whenToUse: Use HStack for horizontal rows (e.g. title + badge, icon + label, action bars).
Use spacing tokens to define gaps between elements.
Use wrap={true} on narrow containers to prevent content from clipping offscreen.
whenNotToUse: Never use HStack when items need to stack vertically on mobile; use wrap={true} or conditional direction.
Never apply manual marginRight to children inside an HStack.
accessibilityNotes: Preserves logical left-to-right reading order for screen readers.
Divider elements inside HStack automatically receive accessibilityRole="none".

components.name: VStack
components.description: Vertical stack layout enforcing consistent spacing between vertical elements with optional divider injection.
whenToUse: Use VStack for vertical column layouts (form fields, card sections, screen bodies).
Use spacing tokens to enforce consistent vertical rhythm (spacing="4" for 16pt, spacing="6" for 24pt).
Use divider for separating list items or summary rows.
whenNotToUse: Never apply manual marginBottom to children inside a VStack.
Never nest dozens of deep empty VStacks; keep layout hierarchies lean.
accessibilityNotes: Preserves top-to-bottom reading flow for assistive accessibility services.

components.name: Divider
components.description: Decorative or semantic separator line with tokenized hairline thickness, subtle border colors, and spacing insets.
whenToUse: Use Divider to visually separate distinct content groups (e.g. between form sections or waybill items).
Use orientation="vertical" inside horizontal headers or action bars.
Use inset tokens to align dividers with container padding.
whenNotToUse: Never use Divider where spacing alone provides adequate visual separation.
Never use raw hex colors or arbitrary height numbers for separators.
accessibilityNotes: Divider defaults to accessibilityRole="none" so decorative lines do not clutter screen reader announcements.

props.name: inset
props.description: Inset padding on start/end using spacing scale

components.name: Text
components.description: Accessible typography primitive with 6 semantic variants, automated header roles, Dynamic Type protection, and WCAG AA contrast.
whenToUse: Use semantic variants (display, heading, title, body, label, caption) instead of overriding font sizes.
Always keep allowFontScaling enabled for accessibility compliance.
Use caption for metadata like timestamps, barcodes, and waybill numbers.
whenNotToUse: Never use raw hex colors or inline style fontSize on Text.
Never disable allowFontScaling to fix card layouts; adjust card flex/padding instead.
accessibilityNotes: Heading and display variants automatically apply accessibilityRole="header" for screen reader navigation.
Default maxFontSizeMultiplier of 2.0 accommodates low-vision warehouse workers without breaking layout flow.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description: Maximum scaling multiplier for Dynamic Type / large font accessibility (default: 2.0)

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description: Whether font automatically scales with device accessibility settings (default: true)

components.name: Icon
components.description: Tokenized wrapper around Lucide icons mapping design system sizes, semantic colors, and screen reader accessibility roles.
whenToUse: Use Icon to render Lucide iconography with design system size tokens (xs, sm, md, lg, xl).
Use semantic color tokens (primary, secondary, brand, success, danger) matching the surrounding context.
Provide an accessibilityLabel when the icon conveys standalone visual meaning.
whenNotToUse: Never use standalone clickable icons without wrapping in IconButton (which enforces 44pt touch targets).
Never hardcode raw icon pixel sizes or raw hex colors.
accessibilityNotes: Icons without accessibilityLabel default to decorative state and are ignored by screen readers.
Icons with accessibilityLabel receive accessibilityRole="image".

props.name: size
props.description: Size token from component tokens (xs: 12, sm: 16, md: 20, lg: 24, xl: 32) or numeric

props.name: color
props.description: Semantic text color token or color string

components.name: Button
components.description: Primary action primitive built on usePressable with Reanimated UI-thread micro-interactions, loading states, and WCAG AA contrast.
whenToUse: Use primary for the single most important action on a screen (e.g. Complete Delivery).
Use secondary or tertiary for auxiliary actions (e.g. View Manifest, Cancel).
Use danger for destructive, irreversible operations (e.g. Delete Waybill).
Use the loading prop during background network submissions to prevent double taps.
whenNotToUse: Never place two primary buttons in the same container; use primary + secondary.
Never shrink buttons below size="sm" (44pt touch target) on mobile screens.
Never allow buttons to stretch vertically in parent rows or flex containers.
accessibilityNotes: Button automatically manages accessibilityRole="button" and accessibilityState={{ disabled, busy: loading }}.
Uses Reanimated snappy spring physics on the native UI thread, respecting system reduced-motion settings.
All size variants guarantee at least a 44x44pt tappable area.

props.name: size
props.description: Size tier enforcing minimum 44pt touch targets (default: 'md')

props.name: loading
props.description: Whether the button is currently in a loading state

props.name: leftIcon
props.description: Optional icon name (e.g. 'ChevronRight', 'Sun'), LucideIcon component, or React element rendered before label

props.name: rightIcon
props.description: Optional icon name (e.g. 'ChevronRight', 'Sun'), LucideIcon component, or React element rendered after label

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Whether the button expands to fill parent container width

props.name: style
props.description: Custom style overrides for button container

props.name: textStyle
props.description: Custom style overrides for text label

components.name: IconButton
components.description: Touch-optimized 44x44 icon button with compile-time mandatory accessibility labels and UI-thread spring physics.
whenToUse: Use IconButton for compact secondary actions in headers, toolbars, and card action clusters (e.g. Print, Filter, Close).
Always supply a descriptive accessibilityLabel describing the action (mandatory at compile-time).
Use variant="ghost" for low-emphasis toolbar icons and variant="primary" or "secondary" for floating buttons.
whenNotToUse: Never use IconButton for the screen's main primary call-to-action; use Button with text label.
Never omit accessibilityLabel, as screen readers cannot announce unlabeled icons.
accessibilityNotes: TypeScript enforces accessibilityLabel at compile time on IconButtonProps.
Guarantees at least a 44x44pt touch target on all size tiers to satisfy WCAG AA 2.5.5.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Screen reader accessibility label - STRICTLY MANDATORY for icon buttons

props.name: size
props.description: Size tier enforcing minimum 44x44pt touch targets (default: 'md')

props.name: shape
props.description: Button shape ('square' with radius.md or 'circle' with radius.full) (default: 'square')

props.name: loading
props.description: Whether the button is in a loading state

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: Accessibility hint describing the action outcome
props.example: accessibilityHint="Sends waybill PDF to connected printer"

components.name: TextField
components.description: Accessible text input built on useTextField with error association, secure text toggles, and tokenized border states.
whenToUse: Always provide a visible label or accessibilityLabel for screen reader clarity.
Use error to communicate specific validation failures (e.g. invalid format).
Use prefix/suffix elements to hint at the input format (e.g. MapPin for address, Search for filtering).
whenNotToUse: Never rely solely on placeholder text as a label, as it disappears when typing.
Never hide error messages without announcing them via accessibilityHint.
accessibilityNotes: TextField binds error text directly to accessibilityHint so screen readers announce errors immediately upon focus.
Enforces a minimum 44pt touch height to satisfy WCAG AA target size criteria.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Helper hint text displayed below the field

props.name: error
props.description: Error state or explicit error message

props.name: prefix
props.description: Prefix element or icon rendered before input

props.name: suffix
props.description: Suffix element or icon rendered after input

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description: Whether the field is for sensitive input

props.name: showSecureToggle
props.description: Whether to show a toggle eye button for secure text entry (default: false)

props.name: size
props.description: Size tier enforcing minimum 44pt touch targets (default: 'md')

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Custom style for the field container (including label and helper)

props.name: inputStyle
props.description: Custom style for the input box

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Ternary selection primitive supporting checked, unchecked, and indeterminate (mixed) states with Reanimated spring physics.
whenToUse: Use Checkbox when users can select zero, one, or multiple options from a list (e.g. shipment filters).
Use indeterminate={true} for parent "Select All" controls when a subset of children are selected.
Provide clear label text describing the selection.
whenNotToUse: Never use Checkbox for mutually exclusive single-select options; use Radio or SegmentedOption.
Never use Checkbox for instantaneous settings changes; use Switch instead.
accessibilityNotes: Checkbox automatically manages accessibilityRole="checkbox" and accessibilityState={{ checked: indeterminate ? "mixed" : checked }}.
Meets WCAG AA touch target criteria by expanding the tappable container beyond the visual box to 44pt.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Whether the checkbox is in an indeterminate (partially selected) state

components.name: Switch
components.description: Binary toggle primitive with Reanimated UI-thread spring physics (motion.spring.snappy) and reduced-motion fallback.
whenToUse: Use switches for instantaneous binary state settings (e.g. Turn on Geofencing, Dark Mode).
Provide clear affirmative labels describing what happens when turned on.
Ensure the switch track and thumb maintain WCAG AA contrast against card backgrounds.
whenNotToUse: Never use a switch when a user must submit the change via a "Save" button; use Checkbox instead.
Never invert the meaning (e.g. "Disable Notifications" switched to ON).
accessibilityNotes: Switch applies accessibilityRole="switch" and accessibilityState={{ checked }}.
The thumb translates across the track using Reanimated on the UI thread, instantly disabling animation if useReducedMotion() is active.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label text placed alongside the switch

components.name: Card
components.description: Surface container primitive supporting outlined, elevated, and filled variants with composable header, content, and footer slots.
whenToUse: Use elevated cards to lift interactive items (e.g. delivery run sheet items) off the background canvas.
Use composable CardHeader, CardContent, and CardFooter to enforce standard section spacing.
Use variant="outlined" for secondary summary information.
whenNotToUse: Never nest cards inside cards with matching borders or shadows.
Never set arbitrary pixel margins on Card; wrap in Stack or Box.
accessibilityNotes: Cards organize content logically so screen readers navigate sequential shipment details naturally.
Ensure text inside cards maintains WCAG AA contrast against card background surfaces in both light and dark modes.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using tokenized card padding scale (default: 'md')

components.name: CardHeader
components.description: Card slot component grouping title and action elements at the top of a Card with tokenized bottom margin.
whenToUse: Use CardHeader as the first child of a Card to contain title, subtitle, and badge or action icons.
whenNotToUse: Never place primary full-width buttons inside CardHeader; use CardFooter instead.
accessibilityNotes: Group header elements so screen readers announce title and badge status first.

components.name: CardContent
components.description: Card slot component holding the primary body elements of a Card.
whenToUse: Use CardContent for the main payload of a card (descriptions, milestone details, summary metrics).
whenNotToUse: Never place sticky card action buttons in CardContent; place them in CardFooter.
accessibilityNotes: Ensures sequential reading order between CardHeader and CardFooter.

components.name: CardFooter
components.description: Card slot component holding auxiliary metadata and action buttons at the bottom of a Card.
whenToUse: Use CardFooter for bottom-anchored actions (e.g. Track Live, View Manifest, ETA labels).
whenNotToUse: Never place card titles or badges in CardFooter.
accessibilityNotes: Ensures screen readers reach action buttons after hearing card content.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Semantic status indicator with guaranteed WCAG AA contrast (≥ 4.5:1), optional status dots, and leading icons.
whenToUse: Use semantic variants according to their true feedback state (success=green, warning=amber, danger=red, brand=blue).
Use the dot prop when status represents live or changing operational states.
Keep badge text concise (1 to 3 words) for quick mobile scanning by couriers.
whenNotToUse: Never use danger badges for non-critical information.
Never use raw hex colors or inline background styles for badges.
accessibilityNotes: Every badge foreground and background pairing meets or exceeds WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast.
Badge applies accessibilityRole="text" so screen readers speak status clearly without announcing it as a button.

props.name: dot
props.description: Whether to render a colored status dot before the label (default: false)

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon component or icon name rendered before the label

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: Content placeholder primitive using Reanimated UI-thread pulse micro-interactions with automated static fallback for vestibular comfort.
whenToUse: Use Skeleton loaders during asynchronous data fetching to reduce perceived latency.
Match skeleton geometry to the exact layout of the arriving content (text, avatar, cards).
Compose multiple skeletons into composite card placeholders.
whenNotToUse: Never use animated skeletons for fast synchronous operations (< 150ms).
Never invent arbitrary flashing animations; use the built-in pulse variant.
accessibilityNotes: Skeleton applies accessibilityRole="none" and accessibilityLabel="Loading content" with accessibilityState={{ busy: true }}.
Automatically respects system reduce-motion settings by halting pulse animation and presenting a static tone.

props.name: height
props.description: Height dimension (default: 16 for text, 48 for rectangular/circular)

components.name: Timeline
components.description: Vertical milestone stepper for courier deliveries and logistics tracking waybills with accessible list semantics and active focus rings.
whenToUse: Use Timeline to structure sequential logistics workflows (e.g. pickup -> sort -> transit -> delivery).
Mark exactly one active in-progress milestone as state="current".
Provide timestamps to reassure customers about delivery recency.
whenNotToUse: Never use Timeline for non-chronological or parallel tasks.
Never skip milestone steps without marking preceding steps completed.
accessibilityNotes: Timeline applies accessibilityRole="list" and marks each item with spoken step numbers (e.g. "Step 2 of 4, current: Sorted at Hub").
Ensures users of assistive technologies understand exactly where an order is along its transit route.

components.name: Chip
components.description: Interactive pill-shaped selection control with 44pt minimum touch target, active brand styling, and visible focus indicator.
whenToUse: Use Chip for interactive selection pills, filter toggles, or compact tag selection.
Use for standalone filter pills or within custom filter bars.
whenNotToUse: Never use raw Pressable or TouchableOpacity for pills or filter toggles.
Do not use Chip as a pure read-only indicator; use Badge instead.
accessibilityNotes: Enforces minimum 44pt touch target and announces accessibilityState selected and disabled.
Adapts accessibilityRole to radio or checkbox when orchestrated within ChipGroup.

props.name: label
props.description: Text label displayed inside the chip

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the chip is currently selected

props.name: size
props.description: Size tier enforcing minimum 44pt touch targets (default: 'md')

props.name: leftIcon
props.description: Optional leading icon name (e.g. 'Tag', 'Check'), Lucide component, or React element

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility role override (default: 'button', or 'radio' / 'checkbox' in groups)

components.name: ChipGroup
components.description: Orchestrates collections of Chips with single or multiple selection, automatic flex wrapping or horizontal scrolling, and ARIA radiogroup/checkbox compliance.
whenToUse: Selectable options use ChipGroup, never raw Pressable.
Use ChipGroup for shipment run-sheet status filters, parcel size pickers, and category selectors.
Use mode="single" for mutually exclusive filters, and mode="multiple" for multi-tag filters.
whenNotToUse: Never roll custom flex-wrap Pressable rows for selectable options; always use ChipGroup.
Do not use for binary switches; use Switch or Checkbox instead.
accessibilityNotes: Applies accessibilityRole="radiogroup" in single mode, and manages screen reader option roles automatically.
Guarantees all child items maintain 44pt minimum touch targets.

props.name: mode
props.description: Selection mode: 'single' for mutually exclusive, 'multiple' for multi-select (default: 'single')

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selection value (single: T | null; multiple: T[])

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled initial value (single: T | null; multiple: T[])

props.name: options
props.description: Available chip options when using data-driven rendering

props.name: size
props.description: Size tier passed down to chips (default: 'md')

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the entire group is disabled

props.name: scrollable
props.description: Whether to render chips in a horizontally scrollable container instead of wrapping (default: false)

props.name: allowEmpty
props.description: Whether deselecting the active item is allowed in single mode (default: false)

components.name: QuantityStepper
components.description: Accessible stepped numeric counter with 44pt touch targets on plus/minus buttons, boundaries clamping, and VoiceOver adjustable support.
whenToUse: Quantities use QuantityStepper, never raw text inputs or +/- buttons.
Use for pallet quantities, package counts, weight tiers, and cargo unit adjustments.
Set min, max, and step boundaries to prevent invalid quantities.
whenNotToUse: Never use raw text inputs or custom +/- buttons for numeric item counters.
Do not use for continuous or wide-range inputs (e.g. monetary amounts); use TextField instead.
accessibilityNotes: Implements accessibilityRole="adjustable" and VoiceOver increment/decrement actions.
Plus and minus buttons guarantee 44x44pt touch targets and disable automatically at bounds.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label displayed above the stepper control

props.name: unit
props.description: Optional unit text displayed beside the number (e.g. 'kg', 'items', 'pallets')

props.name: onChange
props.description: Change callback with updated numeric count
